newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Berisford faces possible bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Berisford faces possible bid.

text.p: Shares in British consumer food equipment to agri-business group Berisford Plc rode high on Friday after it disclosed it had received a takeover approach and despite reporting a dip in annual profits.
Berisford said it had received a "formal interest" in an offer being made for the company.
It said the approach "had been only of a preliminary nature such that it is unclear whether it may or may not lead to an offer being made".
Company chief executive Alan Bowkett said Berisford would not consider any possible bid offer for the firm unless it fitted into its expansion plans.
"I am committed to taking the company forward, the expansion. I have not requested an offer, it has come," Bowkett said in a telephone interview, without commenting on the identity of the buyer.
Berisford's share price shot up to 154 pence from Thursday's close of 121 pence before ending the day slightly off at 152.
This contrasted with a dip in pre-tax profits for the year ended September 28 to 25.5 million pounds ($43 million) from 26.8 million the previous year.
Analysts covering the company said it would attract a price tag of 175 to 200 pence a share, valuing the company at 300 to 365 million pounds, if the bid offer is launched.
One sector analyst at a British broker said: "At today's earnings, I would see a price of around 200 pence a share."
Analysts who met Berisford management at a meeting called by the company to outline its full year results said executives were tight-lipped over the name of the potential buyer.
Swedish consumer goods manufacturer AB Electrolux was hotly tipped by them as a likely suitor, given its estimated cash reserves of more than 600 million pounds.
The prize jewel in Berisford's crown is its U.S. catering equipment subsidiary Welbilt Corporation which accounts for nearly 60 percent of its turnover.
"That makes Electrolux a strong contender, given its presence in the U.S.," said another analyst.
British manufacturers Tomkins Plc and Wassal Plc were also named by analysts as potential buyers.
Bowkett said Berisford's Welbilt unit in the United States was expanding in Latin America and Far East markets and he would ensure that these plans went ahead.
"I have to see that it (expansion) goes forward. These are real matters," Bowkett said.
Analysts said the only factor that could influence the current management to sell was sluggishness in the consumer food equipment industry in Britain and the U.S.

The British sector suffers from overcapacity. In the U.S. some of Welbilt's main clients, the restaurant giants, have failed to expand into mainland Europe and Asia at the pace expected three years ago.
The company, however, said it had fared better in the first seven weeks of the current financial year with sales and orders at Welbilt rising one and eight percent respectively.
It said sales at its British-based Magnet home-improvement unit were up 11 percent, retail kitchen orders were up 19 percent while direct kitchen sales rose eight percent.
When asked whether the company was under any sort of pressure from institutional shareholders to change management, Bowkett said: "We could still grow without any change in management".
The company said the possible offer made its proposed buy-back of convertible unsecured loan stock impracticable until the situation had been clarified. $1=.5937 Pound
